title: Pricing Harness – Client Input
description: One product's price/cost input for the Pricing Engine. null = UNKNOWN (not yet entered), 0 = confirmed zero, a number = an entered value. This wrapping is intentionally NOT used here (see analysis_result.schema.json for the {value,status,unit} pattern, which applies only to computed outputs).

pricing_model.description: Overall shape of the product's pricing. Must be consistent with the types present in price_components.

vat_rate.description: null = unknown. Whether this rate is even needed for a given price_component depends on that component's price_includes_vat flag — see core/schemas/dependency_rules.md.

base_currency.description: Currency most cost items are denominated in, e.g. "KRW".

reporting_currency.description: Currency Analysis Result / Dashboard / Report will show, e.g. "USD".

rate_base_per_reporting.description: How many units of base_currency equal 1 unit of reporting_currency. null = unknown. Set to 1 when base_currency == reporting_currency.

targets.description: target_contribution_margin_rate is used by MODE B and MODE C (global — the same rate applies to every price_component; per-component override not implemented). There is deliberately no target_market_price field here — MODE C's market price is product.price_components[].target_market_price (per-component, so it can differ per component and shares that component's price_includes_vat/currency), not a global scalar. An earlier draft placed a target_market_price field here; it was never read by any implemented mode and has been removed rather than left as an unused, confusingly-named duplicate of the per-component field. Always valid to leave target_contribution_margin_rate null.

evidence.description: Optional provenance for a price or cost value. Used downstream to distinguish Fact / Estimate / Assumption in AI-generated pricing strategy reports.

price_includes_vat.description: null = unknown whether VAT is included. See core/schemas/dependency_rules.md for how this combines with tax.vat_rate.

discount_rate.description: MODE B's single discount rate for inverting required_selling_price into required_list_price on this component: list_price = selling_price / (1 - discount_rate). null = UNKNOWN (required_list_price stays UNKNOWN). 0 = no discount. 0 < rate < 1 = normal. rate >= 1 or a negative rate is a valid *input* but an unsolvable *inversion* — MODE B reports required_list_price as ERROR rather than the schema rejecting the document, so this field is intentionally left unbounded here (unlike cost_item.rate). Distinct from discount_schedule below: discount_schedule is a period/condition-based discount *policy* (multiple rates over time), while discount_rate is the single current-period rate MODE B solves against right now.

target_market_price.description: MODE C's canonical market-price input: the externally-given, effective (discount already applied, if any) transaction selling price for this component — not a pre-discount list price. null = UNKNOWN. 0 = explicit zero (economically unusual but valid — not the same as UNKNOWN). Shares this SAME component's price_includes_vat and currency for VAT-basis/currency interpretation (see common.resolve_price_basis()) — it does not have its own copies of either field. MODE C v0.1 does not read discount_rate against this field; if a future need arises to target-cost against a list price instead, that is a separate addendum, not implemented here. Distinct from actual_price (MODE A's current-price field, which MODE C never reads) and from required_selling_price/required_list_price (MODE B's *outputs*, not an input).

cost_category.description: product_service_direct_cost feeds Gross Profit. variable_selling_delivery feeds Contribution Margin only (not Gross Profit). fixed_operating_cost is excluded from Contribution Margin and used only for BEP / operating-profit estimates.

amount.description: Use for money-valued costs. Leave null and use rate instead for percentage-of-revenue costs.

rate.description: Use for percentage-of-revenue costs (e.g. channel commission, PG fee). Leave null and use amount instead for money-valued costs.

currency.description: null when the item is rate-based (rate has no currency).

basis.description: For cost_category=fixed_operating_cost specifically: basis (typically per_month) states the analysis period this cost figure is already denominated in — it is period CONTEXT for BEP (see docs/features/bep/SPEC.md section 4/12, analysis_result.bep.per_component[].analysis_period_basis), never a quantity unit itself. BEP requires every fixed_operating_cost item it sums for one component to share the same basis (INCONSISTENT_FIXED_COST_BASIS otherwise) — the schema does not enforce this across items, it is a BEP-internal rule.

applies_to_component.description: Must match a product.price_components[].component_id, or the literal "shared" for costs common to all components.

allocation_rule.description: Only meaningful when applies_to_component = "shared". Tells the engine how to split this cost across components: direct = don't split (used as-is where it already applies), by_component_revenue = allocate proportionally to each component's revenue, fixed_share = split by a fixed ratio configured elsewhere, blended_only = never allocated per-component, only appears in the future blended (whole-contract) view. NOTE: 'shared' + 'direct' together is a semantic contradiction ('shared' = not attributed to one component, 'direct' = already attributed to one) — every implemented mode (A/B/C) treats this combination as an invalid configuration (ERROR, code INVALID_ALLOCATION_CONFIGURATION), never as a valid 'use as-is' shortcut. See core/schemas/dependency_rules.md section 4.

frequency_per_year.description: Optional, basis-specific field — e.g. required to annualize a per_visit cost. Not one of the 7 required fields.
